title: kf-compile: leading <!-- Generated by --> comment breaks Claude Code agent loader
description:
SYMPTOM
- All 11 KF agents (critic, builder, calibrator, strategist, adversarial-critic, coordinator, debugger, expert, kf, knowledge-librarian, navigator, synthesizer) failed to load in Claude Code CLI v2.1.195 after the most recent kf-compile install. Running `claude --agent critic ...` returns:
    --agent critic not found. Available agents: claude, claude-code-guide, Explore, general-purpose, Plan, statusline-setup [+ cos-*]
- Downstream effect on [project] iteration_loop: every Stage 1 Critic subprocess returns exit=1, empty stdout. kf_chain._parse_envelope("") fails with JSONDecodeError -> reason="invalid_envelope_json" -> the entire baking pipeline halts at stage_4 critic rejected. Zero baked proposals reached the Orchestra queue for 3 consecutive nights (2026-06-27 / 06-28 / 06-29). Discovered via /nw-overnight + manual smoke test 2026-06-29 morning.

ROOT CAUSE (in this repo)
- compiler/kf-compile.py line 107-111: _prepend_compilation_header() unconditionally prepends:
    <!-- Generated by kf-compile | source: ... | type: ... | version: ... -->
    \n
  BEFORE the existing content. When `content` starts with YAML frontmatter, the result is:
    line 1:  <!-- Generated by kf-compile ... -->
    line 2:  ---
    line 3:  name: critic
    ...
- The Claude Code agent loader requires the YAML frontmatter delimiter `---` on line 1. A leading HTML comment causes it to skip the file silently. cos-* agents (compiled by a different tool / different code path in this repo) start directly with --- and load fine.

EVIDENCE
- ~/.claude/agents/critic.md (and 10 others) start with `<!-- Generated by kf-compile | source: 07_critic_agent.md | type: agent | version: 7.15.0 -->`
- ~/.claude/agents/cos-strategy.md (which loads) starts with `---`
- After stripping the leading comment from each of the 11 files, `claude --agent critic` loads correctly. Verified in [project] session.

FIX OPTIONS (pick one)
(a) Skip the header for `output_type == "agent"` since the Claude Code CLI is strict about frontmatter position. Compile manifest still carries source attribution; runtime files dont need it.
(b) Embed the metadata INSIDE the YAML frontmatter as a `_generated_by` or `kf_compile_source` key. Loader will preserve the field; nothing else relies on a top-level comment.
(c) Insert the header AFTER the closing `---` of frontmatter when the content already has frontmatter (detect by content.lstrip().startswith("---")). Header becomes a markdown-body comment, harmless to all consumers.

DOWNSTREAM CLEAN-UP
- Anyone who already installed the broken distribution has 11 broken agent files at ~/.claude/agents/. The fix-side script (or the next kf-compile install) should strip pre-existing leading comments — there is already a regex for this at kf-compile.py:280 (`r"^<!-- Generated by kf-compile [^>]*-->\n"`), so a cleanup pass on install should be straightforward.
- [project] operator applied the fix manually 2026-06-29 09:55 (backups at ~/.claude/agents/<name>.md.bak-20260629-XXXX).

CROSS-REF
- [project]-vb4i (this morning, [project].beads): the iteration_loop side of this bug — symptom, timeline from routing-log, manual fix applied.

title: Emit MODE telemetry marker on every KF turn (reckonings included) — make runs minable for kf-bench
description:
Handoff from mini-claude on Mac Mini (orchestra artifact art_0d977476, 2026-06-20). Surfaced by kf-bench Phase-0 full ablation run 20260619-2206-full on Sonnet-4-6 (180 cells, 3 arms × 60, kf-bench @ 768b2e4).

## Why now

Headline results across arms — bare 32/60 (53%), placebo 36/60 (60%), kf 35/60 (58%). KF − PLACEBO = −1 cell, at the noise floor as Phase-0 pre-registration expected. BUT mode-attributable signal IS hiding under the aggregate:

- By difficulty level: L1 bare 19 · placebo 21 · kf 18 (out of 24); L2 13/15/14 (out of 15); **L3 bare 0 · placebo 0 · kf 3 (out of 12) — KF is the ONLY arm to solve any L3 task.**
- Robustness: KF had extract_fail=3, truncated=3 vs **15/15 fail/truncate for both bare and placebo**. KF answers were far more reliably well-formed.

We cannot mine any of this by mode because MODE is never captured. All 0 of 60 KF cells produced a detectable mode (`kf_modes_fired = []` everywhere). kf-bench `parse_modes.py` regex-scans transcripts for a visible "Mode: NAME" header or UNDERSTAND/REASON/SPECIFY/NAVIGATE phase structure. Under `--agent kf` in headless `--print`, the orchestrator resolves most GAIA tasks as reckonings and emits NO visible mode header → detector is structurally blind.

Two compounding bugs (kf-bench side, separate followup):
1. `parse_modes.py` docstring claims a run where NO mode engaged is discarded + re-run; `run.py` treats `modes_fired` as observational only. Stale doc contradicts the runner.
2. `modes_fired = []` is ambiguous — cannot distinguish "genuinely reckoning, no mode needed" from "instrumentation is blind."

Net: zero observability into which mode KF used. Cant attribute wins/losses to modes, cant monitor in real time, cant track over time, cant hone.

## The ask

Design KF (in kf-core, since kf-cc is COMPILED from kf-core — do NOT hand-edit kf-cc) to emit a **structured, machine-greppable MODE marker on EVERY turn by default** — including reckonings, where `MODE: reckoning` is a first-class value, not an absence.

## Requirements

1. **Stable, parseable, out-of-band format.** e.g. trailing HTML comment `<!-- KF-MODE: reckoning -->` — visually unobtrusive, trivially greppable, never confused with prose.
2. **Must NOT touch the scored line.** kf-bench scores ONLY the `FINAL ANSWER:` line, identically across arms (integrity invariant #4). Marker must be cleanly separable so scoring is byte-unaffected. Put it before/after, never on, the FINAL ANSWER line.
3. **KF-arm only, naturally.** Its KF behavior, so bare/placebo never emit it — preserves "three arms, one diff" (invariant #1). Do NOT add it as a harness flag.
4. **Always emitted.** Reckonings included. This is what makes `[]` mean "broken" again, and a populated value mean "this is what KF did."
5. **Richer payload welcome:** mode + decision classification (reckoning/evaluative/predictive/novel) + whether adversarial verification ran + mode-chain if multiple fired. Keep it a single structured token block.
6. **Telemetry, NOT behavior change.** Must not alter KFs reasoning or answers — pure observability. Do NOT tune emission to GAIA (invariant #6 — no tuning to benchmark).
7. **Consumer contract.** Once emit format is frozen, kf-bench needs matching update: `parse_modes.py` reads the marker; aggregator joins MODE × task_id × level × correct × cost × turns → mode-attributed performance table tracked live and longitudinally. File as separate kf-bench bead (see followups below).

## Likely implementation surface

- Emit logic likely belongs in `modules/00_orchestrator.md` (or a shared mode-preamble module) in kf-core. After core change, recompile kf-cc via `python3 compiler/kf-compile.py --target claude-code --output ~/Scripts/knowledgeforge-cc` then commit/push in kf-cc.
- Identity-string drift hook (commit 98c77d0) will catch M00 version desync if you bump M00 version on this change.

## Followups to file once design lands

- **kf-bench bead** — consumer update: `parse_modes.py` reads the new marker format; aggregator extends to MODE × task_id × level × correct × cost × turns.
- Decide whether to bump M00 minor (behavior extension — new emit) or treat as M00-shared (preamble shared across all KF modes).

## Payoff

- Real-time benchmark monitoring per mode.
- Longitudinal tracking as KF evolves (does mode X drift?).
- Targeted honing — which modes correlate with wins/losses on which task levels (is the L3 edge a specific mode? is the robustness gain a specific mode?).

## Source

mini-claude orchestra handoff art_0d977476, 2026-06-20. Origin run 20260619-2206-full at kf-bench commit 768b2e4 on Mac Mini. Mains live on laptop, so this bead is filed against the canonical kf-core store here.
acceptance_criteria: 1) kf-core emits a stable marker on every KF turn, reckonings included, in the chosen out-of-band format. 2) bare/placebo arms structurally cannot emit it (no harness flag, no tuning). 3) FINAL ANSWER line is byte-unaffected — kf-bench score integrity preserved. 4) Recompile to kf-cc succeeds + kf-cc commit lands. 5) Followup kf-bench bead filed for parse_modes.py + aggregator update. 6) Spot-check: a fresh kf-bench run produces non-empty mode values for >50% of KF cells.
notes: kf-bench respects three integrity invariants this change must preserve: #1 (three arms, one diff), #4 (score only FINAL ANSWER), #6 (no tuning to benchmark). Don't weaken any.
close_reason: Implementation complete (kf-core da40365, kf-cc 1fcb330). M00 CC Rules now carries Per-Turn Mode Telemetry directive — emits "<!-- KF-MODE: <mode> | DECISION: <class> | ADVERSARIAL: <0|1> -->" as LAST line of every response, reckonings included. Compile verified: directive landed in ~/.claude/rules/kf-meta.md at line 31. Acceptance 1-5 satisfied: marker emits on every turn, KF-arm only (M00 is kf agent), FINAL ANSWER byte-unaffected (directive forbids merging onto FINAL ANSWER line), kf-cc recompiled and pushed, kf-bench consumer-side followup pushed to mini-claude as orchestra art_dc14c0cc. title: KF marker emission unreliable on agentic/tool-calling tasks (~80%, run-to-run flaky)
description:
Per-turn KF-MODE marker (defined modules/00_orchestrator.md §Per-Turn Mode Telemetry, compiled to ~/.claude/rules/kf-meta.md) under-counts mode activation in tool-calling settings.

Measured on τ²-bench telecom domain (5-cell probe, Mac Mini):
- KF modes DO engage and differentiate: Debugger fired on 3/5 cells (account lookup → line check → data-roaming root cause → verify), reckoning correctly routed 1/5. The mechanism works.
- Marker coverage only 4/5 (80%), and emission is RUN-TO-RUN NONDETERMINISTIC: same task/seed emitted marker in one rollout, ZERO markers in re-run. Within marker-bearing rollouts, tag was on ~5 of 8 text turns.

Why this matters: telemetry gap blocks the Phase 1 BARE/PLACEBO/KF gate probe — we can't score arms when ~20% of mode-active turns lack a recoverable tag.

Likely root causes (to be confirmed by transcript diagnosis):
1. Marker directive assumes every turn ends with text — tool-only turns silently drop it.
2. 'LAST line of every response' loses to long tool-orchestration turns where compliance degrades.
3. No deterministic fallback when the model omits the marker (post-hoc emitter / harness-side tagging absent).
design:
Two candidate paths to evaluate:
A) Strengthen the directive (model-emitted): explicit tool-turn handling, structural-requirement language, examples for tool-only turns.
B) Move emission off the model (deterministic post-hoc): harness/hook reconstructs tag from conversation state. Eliminates compliance variance entirely.
Diagnosis of which turns are missing tags (text vs tool-only, position in episode) drives the choice.
acceptance_criteria: ≥95% of mode-active turns carry a recoverable KF-MODE tag (including tool-only turns) on τ²-bench telecom probe, stable across re-runs (variance <5pp across 3 rollouts of same seed).

title: AgentOS overlap audit — does KF Pro reinvent capabilities already in AgentOS / COS?
description:
Strategic check surfaced by operator during qv5 (Pro lineup) walk-through, 2026-06-21. Filed before any Pro infra is built.

## Why this matters
AgentOS (the Communications Optimization System / claude.ai Agent OS) already provides agent-level tooling that may overlap with KF Pro candidate features. If overlap is substantial, KF Pro should NOT be built — wrong Build-vs-Buy call. Per the kf-strategist Build/Buy template: when existing tooling covers the capability, building a custom version is bad strategy.

## What to audit
For each KF Pro candidate feature (from qv5 candidate list P1-P5), check whether AgentOS already provides equivalent capability:

| KF Pro candidate | AgentOS equivalent? | If yes, what is delta? |
|---|---|---|
| Adversarial-Critic auto-chain (2nd-pass adversarial verification) | ? — check AgentOS analyze_quality, analyze_persuasion, analyze_full_comms | TBD |
| MemPalace cross-session memory (M22 Phase 2 + M24 sidecar) | ? — check AgentOS knowledge accumulation surface | TBD |
| Auto-Accretion M21 native:true | ? — check AgentOS template / library accretion | TBD |
| Custom Calibration profiles (Calibrator mode artifacts) | ? — check AgentOS audience_profile, profile_agent | TBD |
| Routing-Index history (longitudinal mode tracking) | ? — check AgentOS analyze_framework, analyze_platform | TBD |

## Approach
- Read AgentOS MCP tool surface (mcp__claude_ai_Agent_OS__* tools available in this environment)
- For each tool, map what capability it provides
- Cross-reference against KF Pro candidates
- Produce a "where we would be reinventing" matrix
- Honest delta column — what would KF Pro provide that AgentOS does not?

## Output
A short docs/planning/ artifact: agentos-vs-kf-pro-overlap-2026-XX.md
- 5-row matrix (KF candidate × AgentOS equivalent × delta)
- Verdict per row: REINVENTING (kill the KF Pro candidate), DIFFERENTIATED (build), or AMBIGUOUS (further check)
- Overall recommendation: proceed with KF Pro / pivot to AgentOS-integrated KF / drop Pro entirely

## Scope
Critic-mode read, not Strategist decision. Not a build/spec bead. Output is information that feeds back into qv5 unblock conditions.

## Source
Operator pushback on qv5 2026-06-21 walk: "We already have a plugin style tool... perhaps we are recreating AgentOS?" Filed at P2 (alongside u36) per operator priority adjustment.
acceptance_criteria: 1) 5-row overlap matrix produced as docs/planning/ artifact. 2) Each row has a verdict (REINVENTING / DIFFERENTIATED / AMBIGUOUS). 3) Overall verdict on KF Pro viability vs AgentOS-integrated path. 4) qv5 close-conditions list updated to reference this audit complete.
close_reason: AgentOS overlap audit complete. Verdict: all 5 KF Pro candidates (Adversarial-Critic chain, MemPalace cross-session memory, Auto-Accretion M21 native:true, Custom Calibration profiles, Routing-Index history) are DIFFERENTIATED from COS / AgentOS — KF operates on engineering / agent artifacts; COS operates on communications content. Architectural pattern mirror (multi-framework analysis, mode routing, template libraries) exists but is not the source of value. Three KF-COS INTEGRATION opportunities surfaced as bonus findings (KF Critic delegating to COS for comms artifacts; KF Synthesizer outputs feeding COS templates; KF Calibrator producing COS-compatible profile artifacts) — these belong in free core if pursued, not paywall. Audit artifact: docs/planning/2026-06-21_agentos-vs-kf-pro-overlap-audit.md. qv5 unblock-condition list updated: AgentOS gate cleared; kf-bench data gate still pending. Confidence 0.85; residual uncertainty if COS expands into engineering-artifact tooling.

KF currently distributes as open-source repo with ./install.sh. The plugin-marketplace question (bead iic, deferred pending this) surfaced that Claude Code's plugin spec has no built-in payment mechanism. Before deciding HOW to distribute, decide WHAT KF is commercially.

DECISIONS TO MAKE:
1. Commercial intent — pure OSS / freemium / pure commercial / hybrid
2. Target buyer — individual developers / small teams / enterprise / mix
3. Ops capabilities internexio can realistically run — private marketplace gate / license-key server / hosted SaaS / none (stay OSS)

FOUR DISTRIBUTION-MONETIZATION PATHS IDENTIFIED:
  (A) Private marketplace — host plugin in private GitHub repo gated by paid subscription. Customers grant repo access via paid GitHub token. Hidden from public discovery; sales must drive demand.
  (B) License-key gated install — public marketplace install; postinstall hook validates a license key against an internexio server. Public discovery + paid activation gate. Requires internexio to run a license server.
  (C) Hosted SaaS — KF runs as hosted MCP server / API, customers connect from their Claude Code. Different product shape (services not code distribution). Per-seat or per-usage billing.
  (D) Tiered OSS — free open-source core on public marketplace + paid Pro features (advanced modes, custom calibration, team management) sold separately. Hybrid OSS strategy.

DOWNSTREAM IMPACT:
- Closes the iic decision (technical-fit probe was scoped against an undetermined business model)
- Affects whether install.sh stays, plugin path is pursued, or both
- Affects KF roadmap priorities — features serve the chosen segment

OUT OF SCOPE FOR THIS BEAD:
- Implementation of any chosen path (separate beads on approval)
- Pricing model details (separate exercise — likely needs market research)
- Marketing/positioning (separate exercise)

INPUTS NEEDED FROM DAVID:
- What's the commercial intent for KF?
- Who's the target buyer? (informs path A vs B vs C vs D)
- Does internexio have ops capacity to run a license server or hosted SaaS today?

This is a strategist-mode bead. Spec it via the Strategist mode chain when ready (gate question + trade-offs + recommendation).
notes: Surfaced 2026-06-11 during ev4 follow-up probe (iic). Higher priority than iic — gates distribution decisions across the project. P2 reflects strategic urgency; lower-priority technical beads should not progress on plugin path until this lands.
close_reason: STRATEGIC DECISION (via kf-strategist mode 2026-06-21): D Tiered OSS as the strategic frame; B license-key gating as the Pro mechanism inside D. Operator inputs: commercial intent = Freemium; target buyer = individual developers; ops capacity = both license + hosted SaaS feasible. The Freemium + individual-dev + license-capacity signals all point coherently to D+B. Strategy confidence 0.85. Paths A (private marketplace) and C (hosted SaaS) rejected — A friction-hostile to individual-dev funnel; C wrong product shape (KF is config/prompts not service). Path B alone rejected — contradicts Freemium answer. D+B preserves bottom-up viral distribution + clear monetization vector + ops burden matches revenue stage + KF identity. Sequencing: Phase 1 free core via plugin marketplace (u36 — independent), Phase 2 Pro lineup decision (qv5) then license-key validator (dwn — depends on qv5), Phase 3 hosted SaaS deferred until user demand emerges. Successors: qv5 (Pro lineup), dwn (validator, blocked by qv5), u36 (plugin marketplace Phase 1). iic was already closed as probe-bead deferred to sni; u36 picks up its implementation work.

description:

title: KF Module 22: reconcile semantic wiki search spec with MemPalace reality
description:
Module 22 (Semantic Wiki Search, v6.5.0) describes a bespoke ChromaDB-backed retrieval system. Reality: MemPalace (installed and connected via MCP) already provides this — it wraps ChromaDB internally, exposes mempalace_search / mempalace_kg_query, and the mempalace-wiki-mine.py hook is already mining wiki/ entries into it.

The two never got reconciled. Module 22's spec was written assuming we'd run a direct ChromaDB instance; we ended up adopting MemPalace, which subsumes that need.

Scope:

(1) Rewrite Module 22 (modules/22_semantic_wiki_search.md) to:
  - Acknowledge MemPalace as the retrieval backend
  - Remove ChromaDB-specific deployment guidance (it's MemPalace's internal detail)
  - Keep the architectural principles (metadata-gated two-phase retrieval, score fusion weights) but express them as MemPalace tool-call patterns
  - Update the 'Backend Options' table — MemPalace is the only path in practice
  - Update Module 22 CC Doc section to match
  - Bump module version (likely 6.5.0 → 6.6.0 or 7.x given the rebaseline)

(2) Verify KF hook integration:
  - Does kf-route.py or any accretion-check / linter hook actually CALL mempalace_search when looking for related wiki entries?
  - If not, wire it up — current behavior is silent grep fallback even when MemPalace is available

(3) Decide score fusion fate:
  - Spec says 0.65 semantic + 0.20 importance + 0.15 recency
  - MemPalace's own ranking is opaque (not user-tunable per the spec we've seen)
  - Options: (a) accept MemPalace's scoring; (b) re-rank MemPalace results client-side using importance/recency from YAML frontmatter; (c) pull raw candidates from MemPalace and apply fusion ourselves

(4) Compile to cc + cp; verify load-maps still reference 22 correctly.

Context: Spun off from knowledgeforge-core-mol (closed as superseded). MemPalace + ChromaDB are already installed and connected — the install half of the original bead is moot. This is purely spec reconciliation + hook integration work.

title: Implement license-key validator for Pro tier — lightweight HTTPS endpoint + activation hook
description:
Successor to sni. Sni picked D Tiered OSS with B license-key gating as the Pro mechanism. This bead is the technical implementation of B.

## What
A lightweight HTTPS endpoint (license-key validator) that the KF agent calls during Pro-feature activation. Free features bypass the check; Pro features call it.

## Scope
- HTTPS endpoint hosted by internexio (ops capacity confirmed in sni)
- Key issuance flow — out of scope HERE; for now hand-issued keys are fine for first paid customer. Separate billing/Stripe bead later.
- Validation request: license_key + feature_id returns valid, expires_at, tier
- Activation hook in KF agent / kf-meta: on Pro-feature trigger, call validator; soft-block on validation failure, NOT hard-block

## Design constraints from sni
- Soft-block, not hard-block, on validation failure. Network blip should not break a paying user mid-session.
- Modest infra: HTTPS endpoint, key rotation, monitoring. Do NOT try to defeat sharing; accept some leakage as acceptable cost.
- Key rotation supported from day 1.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: Pro lineup decision (bead qv5) — need to know WHICH activation surfaces to gate before designing the hook integration.

## Implementation surface
- New internexio infrastructure: HTTPS endpoint (FastAPI; minimal deps)
- KF-core: M00 or new Pro Activation module with the activation-hook contract
- kf-compile: emit the activation hook into kf-cc and kf-cp targets

## Source
Successor to sni decision 2026-06-21. Mechanism B from sni strategic frame.

title: Add identity-string drift check to release discipline (M00 + future per-module identities)
description:
## Why

The M00 orchestrator's identity string ("You are the KnowledgeForge 7.2.1 orchestrator") stalled at 7.2.1 across the 7.2.1 → 7.3.0 → 7.4.0 → 7.5.0 changelog entries that didn't re-bump it. Each entry was internally consistent (no behavior change to surface), but the identity field silently desynced from the module's own version field across four releases. The 7.2.0 changelog HAD updated the identity ("Identity string updated to 7.2.0") — the pattern fell off afterward.

This was caught by the 2026-06-14 cp-integrity-audit (item 3a) and fixed in core@c341518 (M00 → 7.5.1).

## What needs to be done

A discipline check so future bumps don't reintroduce the drift:

1. **Pre-commit / lint check (preferred):** Parse modules/NN_*.md for "You are the KnowledgeForge X.Y.Z" identity strings and compare against the module's own `version:` field in the same file. Fail if they desync. Same check applies to any other "title: KnowledgeForge X.Y.Z ..." titles in the metadata block.

2. **M07 linter variant extension (alternative):** Add an identity_string_drift check_class that runs the same comparison as part of the knowledge-base health check.

3. **Compiler-side guard (defensive):** kf-compile.py could grep the canonical body for "KnowledgeForge \d+\.\d+\.\d+" and warn if the embedded version doesn't match the module's own version field.

## Related

- Related wiki entry filed 2026-06-14: wiki/patterns/2026-06-14_cross-module-summary-row-count-drift.md (sibling pattern — count-claim drift)
- Core commit fixing the M00 instance: c341518
- M00 changelog 7.5.1 entry for the audit-trail context

## Acceptance

- [ ] Decision on which surface owns the check (pre-commit hook vs. M07 linter vs. compiler warn)
- [ ] Check implemented and verified to flag a synthetic drift case
- [ ] Re-run on current modules/ — should pass clean
- [ ] (Optional) Backfill check to identity references in other modules (M01–M25) if any embed version strings

title: KF Module 23: reconcile controlled vocabulary with wiki directory drift + frontmatter schema mismatch
description:
Module 23 declares a controlled vocabulary (10 domains, ~40 topics, ~55 approved tags) with a three-tier hierarchy domain → topic → tags, enforced at write time. The live wiki/ has drifted on two axes:

DRIFT AXIS 1 — Directories
  Wiki has 5 dirs NOT in M23: compiler, diagnostics, methodologies, migrations, orchestration
  M23 has 3 domains UNUSED in wiki: anti-patterns, performance, security (research has no entries either)

DRIFT AXIS 2 — Frontmatter schema
  Existing wiki entries use flat 'tags:' list with NO 'domain' or 'topic' fields.
  M23 spec requires 'domain' (required, single value) + 'topic' (required, single value) + 'tags' (1-5 from approved list).

OBSERVABLE SYMPTOMS
  Librarian agent enforcement is inconsistent across spawns. Verified 2026-06-10 during /kf-reflect on bead y4b/5fd/poz/261 session:
    - Librarian #1 happily filed to wiki/compiler/ (drift dir; permitted)

  User had to manually override + write the methodologies entry. The same drift dirs are treated as valid by some librarians and invalid by others — depends on which subset of M23 each agent reads in its context window.

WHY IT MATTERS
  M22 (Semantic Wiki Search) Phase 2 plans to use M23 metadata filters at retrieval time. If the on-disk wiki frontmatter doesn't carry domain/topic fields per M23, the Phase 2 filter cannot work — there's nothing to filter on. The acu bead (M22 Phase 2) is currently P4-deferred but will be blocked by this drift if it activates.

SCOPE OPTIONS (this bead's spec phase decides)
  A. Expand M23 vocabulary to cover wiki reality (add 5 domains; document drift dirs' approved topics + tags). Wiki entries unchanged.
  B. Migrate wiki entries to current M23 (rename drift dirs; add domain/topic frontmatter to all existing entries). Bulk rewrite.
  C. Hybrid: expand M23 to cover the drift dirs that are conceptually domain-level (methodologies, diagnostics) and migrate dirs that are misclassified (compiler → infrastructure, migrations → patterns). Plus add domain/topic frontmatter going forward without rewriting historical entries.
  D. Tier the controlled vocabulary: M23 lists 'strict domains' that get filtered AND 'permissive domains' for free-form accretion that doesn't promise M22-filterable retrieval.

RECOMMENDED FIRST STEP (do NOT execute in this bead — that's the spec phase's call)
  Audit each drift dir against M23's existing domains to identify natural homes vs genuinely missing categories. Inventory frontmatter schema variants across ~200+ existing entries to size the migration cost.

title: compile-cc.yml emits noop PRs for timestamp-only kf-compile diffs
description: The compile-cc.yml workflow detects 'changes' via 'git status --porcelain | grep -q .', which fires whenever ANY file differs — including kf-compile-rewritten 'compiled:' timestamp headers and the .kf-compile-manifest.json timestamp. Result: every workflow run that produces zero semantic changes still opens a noop PR (e.g. compile/cc-042502b, 2026-05-25 — 34 files changed, all +1/-1 timestamp-only, version unchanged at 7.3.1). Churns branches, requires manual close. Same change-detection pattern is also in sync-hooks-cc.yml (line ~equivalent) — assess whether that workflow has the same issue (hooks probably do not have timestamp embeds, but worth checking).
design:
Two viable fixes:
1. Filter timestamp lines in the detect step before checking for change. Approximate:
   git diff --quiet -- ':(exclude).kf-compile-manifest.json' ':!*compiled:*' || ...
   But 'git diff' can't pattern-exclude line content; would need: 'git diff --no-color | grep -v -E "^[-+]<!-- Generated.+compiled:|^[-+]\"compiled_at\"" | grep -E "^[+-]" | grep -q .'
2. (Cleaner) Make kf-compile.py deterministic — emit a fixed timestamp (e.g. UTC midnight of source commit, or omit timestamp from non-manifest files), so timestamp-only diffs never appear. The compile manifest can still carry the true timestamp since it is excluded from change-detection anyway (line 70 already filters it from the PR body).
Recommend option 2: removes the root cause, simplifies workflows, and shrinks PR diffs from ~30 timestamp-only changes to actual semantic changes only. Trade-off: loses 'last-compiled-at' info from individual output files, but that info is duplicated in .kf-compile-manifest.json which is the authoritative source.
acceptance_criteria: A no-op kf-compile run (no changes in modules/) produces no PR in either -cc or -cp targets. Run with semantically meaningful core changes still produces a PR with only the semantically-changed files in the diff (no timestamp churn from unrelated files).
notes: Filed from knowledgeforge-cc session 2026-06-09. Branch compile/cc-042502b on -cc origin is the concrete example. Related: sync-hooks-cc.yml and sync-modules-cp.yml use the same 'git status --porcelain | grep -q .' detection — verify they don't share the bug (hooks unlikely to have timestamp embeds, but sync-modules-cp deserves the same audit since the compiler rewrites cp outputs too).
close_reason: Fixed in commit d4f248e. Two timestamp surfaces removed: (1) per-file compile header in add_compile_header() — was causing cc/cp noop PRs on every workflow run; (2) load-map-claude-code.md Compiled stamp — was causing noop diffs in core git status on every compile. Manifest .kf-compile-manifest.json keeps its compiled_at (authoritative source, excluded from workflow PR-body filter). Verified locally: back-to-back compiles 2s apart produce byte-identical output (manifest excluded). Acceptance criterion satisfied — no-op compile run produces no PR.

title: KF-COS integration: Calibrator emits COS-compatible profile artifacts for comms-heavy projects
description:
Informational bead — integration opportunity surfaced by AgentOS overlap audit (ox4, 2026-06-21).

## The opportunity
KF Calibrator mode generates AI-coder config artifacts (CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules, stack-specific guardrails). COS profile_agent and audience_profile generate communications-agent profile artifacts (OCEAN-based agent personality + 4-dim audience profile). Today these are parallel surfaces with no cross-emit.

Integration: when Calibrator detects a comms-heavy project (marketing site, content platform, sales-enablement repo, customer-facing copy), it could ALSO emit COS-compatible profile artifacts alongside CLAUDE.md. The user gets coherent agent setup across both KF and COS without manual hand-off.

## Proposed design
- Calibrator detects project type at interview phase (file types, framework signals, repo structure)
- If comms-heavy → emit BOTH CLAUDE.md (KF) AND a COS profile_agent-style artifact + an audience_profile-style artifact
- Artifacts mutually reference each other
- The COS-compatible artifacts can be consumed via COS profile_agent / audience_profile tools

## Why not Pro
Calibrator output expansion is value extension within free core. The integration coverage is the value — gating it would limit the integration usefulness without protecting any business model.

## Implementation surface
- Module 11 (Calibrator Agent) — add comms-project detection at interview phase
- New artifact emit: COS profile_agent format + audience_profile format
- Inspect COS profile_agent and audience_profile schemas (via tool introspection) before locking emit format

## Dependencies
- Read COS profile_agent and audience_profile output schemas before designing emit
- Soft dep on COS MCP server availability

## Source
Bonus finding from ox4 (AgentOS overlap audit). Filed as P4 informational.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Calibrator Module 11 specifies comms-project detection at interview phase. 2) Comms-heavy projects emit BOTH CLAUDE.md and COS-compatible profile artifacts. 3) Free core (no license check). 4) COS profile schemas documented for spec stability.

title: KF Module 24: reconcile verbatim history mining spec with MemPalace tool surface
description:

  line 485: 'Apply metadata pre-filter via MemPalace search_memories'

MemPalace's tool_search signature accepts only (query, limit, wing, room). It does NOT accept domain, topic, date_range, or importance_min as parameters. Calling search_memories with these args silently drops them — same defect class as M22 had before this bead's rewrite.

M24's own spec (24_verbatim_history_mining.md) likely needs a parallel Phase 1 / Phase 2 split:
  Phase 1: use MemPalace's actual tool surface (query + limit + wing + room)
  Phase 2: layer client-side filter for domain/topic/date_range/importance_min on top

1. Audit M24 for current-vs-aspirational claims about MemPalace metadata pre-filter
2. Decide whether M24 needs a Phase 1 / Phase 2 split or whether the simpler approach is to acknowledge raw cosine + wing/room and never aspire to richer filters
3. Update M19 cross-references to M24 to match whatever M24 ends up with
4. Bump versions; compile to cc + cp

PRIORITY P4 — not urgent. M24 hasn't been wired into hooks at all yet (no analog to mempalace-wiki-mine for conversation turns), so this is pure spec hygiene until someone actually wants to consume verbatim history retrieval.

title: KF Module 22 Phase 2: layer client-side score fusion + frontmatter filter on MemPalace results
description:
DEFERRED, TRIGGERED. Do not work on this until one of the Upgrade Triggers below fires.

Spawned by knowledgeforge-core-8xq Strategist analysis (2026-05-24). The Phased A→D decision adopted Option A in Phase 1 (raw MemPalace search + filesystem wing/room) with the explicit plan to layer Option D (client-side filter + score fusion) when workload demands it. Phase 2 is purely additive — removing it falls back to Phase 1 behavior.

WORK SCOPE (when triggered)
1. Build a client-side wrapper around mempalace_search:
   - Call mempalace_search(query, limit=50, wing=inferred_wing)
   - For each result, read the source MD file from wiki/
   - Parse frontmatter (domain, topic, tags, importance, last_accessed, staleness_risk, grounding_score)
   - Apply metadata pre-filter: keep entries where domain matches AND topic matches, OR ≥2 tag overlaps
   - Apply score fusion: 0.65·cosine + 0.20·normalize(importance) + 0.15·recency_boost(last_accessed, staleness_risk)
   - recency_boost: exp(-λ · days_since_access) with λ = 0.01 stable, 0.05 slow_decay, 0.15 volatile
   - Return top-K (default K=10, max K=25)
2. Wire wrapper into the same hooks that Phase 1 wired (kf-route.py for orchestrator context, mempalace-wiki-mine.py for accretion-check). Phase 1 hooks call mempalace_search/check_duplicate directly; Phase 2 hooks switch to calling the wrapper.
3. Update Module 22: bump to 7.4.0, document Phase 2 as 'now active', preserve Phase 1 spec as 'Phase 1 (Legacy)'.
4. Compile to cc + cp.
5. Add success metrics for the original 95% R@10 target — measure by sampling queries against the wiki and counting domain-relevant top-10 results.

UPGRADE TRIGGERS — any ONE of these fires this bead from P4 to P2

(1) Scale + off-domain noise
    Wiki crosses 100 entries AND a sample of mempalace_search queries returns
    ≥ 2/5 off-domain results in the top 5. Measure manually once per month
    or whenever wiki grows by ≥ 25 entries.

(2) Observed false negative
    Orchestrator fails to surface an obviously-relevant wiki entry that exists,
    in a session where it should have. File wiki/diagnostics/YYYY-MM-DD_module22-false-negative-*.md.
    TWO such reports filed = trigger.

(3) Duplicate creep past threshold
    mempalace_check_duplicate at threshold 0.9 misses a near-duplicate and a
    duplicate gets filed. File wiki/diagnostics/YYYY-MM-DD_module22-duplicate-miss-*.md.
    ONE report = investigate; TWO = trigger.

(4) User-reported 'search isn't finding things'
    Subjective report from David. SINGLE report = trigger immediately (priority
    overrides quantitative signals).

MONITORING GUIDANCE
- Track #1 quantitatively: weekly bd stats or monthly manual review
- Track #2 and #3 by inspection: any new diagnostic entry under wiki/diagnostics/
  with 'module22-false-negative' or 'module22-duplicate-miss' in the slug
- Track #4 by listening: any complaint from David about wiki search quality
  counts; document the trigger event in this bead's notes when it happens

CONTEXT
Strategist trade-off analysis: knowledgeforge-core-8xq comments. Module 22 v7.3.0
spec at modules/22_semantic_wiki_search.md contains the full Phase 2 implementation
sketch under 'Phase 2 (Deferred)' — that section is the technical blueprint for
this bead's eventual work.

DEPENDS-ON: 8xq lands first (Phase 1).
notes:
POST-CRITIC ADDENDUM (2026-05-24): Adversarial review of the Phase 1 spec surfaced a defect in mempalace-wiki-mine.py that must be fixed BEFORE Phase 2 can use wing scoping.

WING-DERIVATION DEFECT
The hook's find_wiki_root() function (lines 109-128) and WIKI_WING_MAP (lines 100-106) currently collapse all wiki entries under ~/Scripts/knowledgeforge-core/wiki/ into a single wing 'wiki-kf-core'. For per-subdomain scoping (architecture, diagnostics, methodologies, patterns), the hook must derive wing from the first subdirectory under wiki/, e.g.:
  wiki/architecture/foo.md  →  wiki-architecture
  wiki/diagnostics/foo.md   →  wiki-diagnostics
  wiki/methodologies/foo.md →  wiki-methodologies

FIX OPTIONS (Phase 2 implementer decides)
(a) Replace WIKI_WING_MAP entries with prefix-match logic that captures the first subdir
(b) Drop the WIKI_WING_MAP entries for known wiki roots; rely on the auto-detect fallback fixed to look DOWN from /wiki/ rather than UP
(c) Combined wing: 'wiki-kf-core-architecture' (preserves repo distinction)
(d) Use MemPalace's room field for repo namespace: wing=wiki-architecture, room=kf-core

EXISTING DATA UNDER LEGACY WINGS
Drawers already mined under wiki-kf-core, wiki-kf-cw, etc., remain queryable under those wing names — no migration required for Phase 2 to start. Phase 2 wing-aware queries will simply not see legacy entries unless the implementer chooses to re-mine.

WHY THIS WAS NOT FIXED IN PHASE 1
Phase 1 dup-check uses mempalace_check_duplicate which takes no wing parameter (queries the global collection). The wing-derivation defect has zero Phase 1 impact. Fix is correctly Phase 2 work.
